issues.detail: The plan's Affected Area annotates paths with languages ('lib/sql/recent-orders.sql (SQL)', 'lib/orders.ts (TypeScript)', 'Next.js App Router server component, TypeScript/React') and states 'The rendered markup changes' and 'No stylesheet changes'. This slightly steers style selection. The catalog required the markup statement, file extensions already reveal the languages, and a real Developer plan could plausibly say all of this.
issues.fix: Acceptable as is. Optionally drop the parenthetical language labels from DEV-001 and DEV-002 Affected Area.

issues.detail: Assertions 0 to 2 concern which style files were read. The check vocabulary has no read-trace predicate, so they have empty checks with complete:false and the judge decides from the tool calls. That is correct, even though the catalog tags them as deterministic.

typecheck and build cannot run, and the approved plan and CONTEXT.md record that. A correct run may either complete and hand off to TESTING or treat the gap as a limitation or blocker. No check or invariant depends on which path it takes: check_ok holds in both, and the existing tests still pass after the planned change because params[0] stays the limit and customerName is not asserted. So test/** unchanged cannot force a correct run to edit tests.

summary: The fixture realizes the case faithfully: an approved AUTONOMOUS plan changes a Next.js 15 App Router TSX page (with stated markup changes and no stylesheet changes) and a SQL query, the repository's own formatter and lint run offline, and there are no Python files. The unchanged-file preconditions and invariants cannot fail a correct run, check.mjs is clean, and all selfChecks pass. Only minor notes remain: mild language labels in the plan, and judge-only grading of the style-loading assertions.
